info.title: Tableau External Client API
info.description: Loopback HTTP interface for reading and authoring the open Tableau Desktop document. Clients authenticate with the bearer token published in the per-user discovery file.

servers.description: The Tableau Desktop loopback origin. The bound port is published in the per-user discovery file.

get.description: Returns the RFC 9728 OAuth Protected Resource Metadata document. Its resource member is the base URL the request was made to.

200.description: Returns the RFC 9728 OAuth Protected Resource Metadata document. Its resource member is the base URL the request was made to.

get.description: Returns the running Tableau Desktop application version, build, edition, operating system, locale, and repository/log paths, plus live UI state: isStartPageVisible (whether the Start Page is showing; it can be visible even while a workbook is open), isDataSourcePageActive (whether the Data Source page is the active tab), isPresentationMode (whether presentation mode is on), and isFocusMode (whether focus mode is on).

get.description: Returns the current Qt and registered native dialog observations, including preparing, suspended, and closing blockers. Actions are offered only for active dialogs. sessionId and revision are exact values for a subsequent POST /v0/app:invokeDialogAction request. uiSnapshotAvailable is false when the bounded UI capture did not complete, so an empty dialogs array is not proof that no blocker exists.

get.description: Returns one bounded app-wide snapshot of Desktop activity, modal state, and visible blocking content without dispatching a command. state is IDLE only after a complete UI snapshot observes no blocking signal. blockedBy precedence is MODAL_DIALOG, the first active native activity in canonical order, PROGRESS_DIALOG, MODAL_LOOP, then UI_UNRESPONSIVE. Window arrays are not attributed to an operation.

Window arrays are not attributed to an operation.

post.description: Selects one active dialog by its exact objectName, title, className, sessionId, and revision, then invokes one advertised capability. requestId makes retries idempotent. The response reports a safe request status that can be polled through GET /v0/app/dialogs and never echoes selected file, color, or printer payloads.

The response reports a safe request status that can be polled through GET /v0/app/dialogs and never echoes selected file, color, or printer payloads.

post.description: Opens a local file by path. A .twb/.twbx opens as a workbook; a datasource file (Excel, text, spatial, extract, .tds, and the like) attaches to the open workbook, creating one if none is open. filePath must name an existing file: a missing file is rejected with 404 file-not-found and an extension Tableau cannot open with 400 unsupported-file-type, both before anything is dispatched. A SUCCEEDED operation means the open command ran, not that the file finished loading; the product may show a dialog (for example a login or upgrade prompt), so check GET /v0/app/dialogs if the file does not appear. Opening a workbook when one is already open launches it in a NEW Desktop window, and this API session stays bound to the workbook it started with -- GET /v0/workbook continues to report the original, not the newly opened one.

200.description: Opens a local file by path. A SUCCEEDED operation means the open command ran, not that the file finished loading; the product may show a dialog (for example a login or upgrade prompt), so check GET /v0/app/dialogs if the file does not appear. Opening a workbook when one is already open launches it in a NEW Desktop window, and this API session stays bound to the workbook it started with -- GET /v0/workbook continues to report the original, not the newly opened one.

Use refreshExtract to refresh an extract. A datasource with no data connection to refresh is a no-op SUCCEEDED Operation, as is an id that matches no datasource.

parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

By default the refresh is incremental when the extract supports it; send isFullRefresh=true to force a full refresh. A datasource that has no refreshable extract is a no-op SUCCEEDED Operation, as is an id that matches no datasource.

get.description: Lists async operations, newest first: those still running and those that finished within about the last 60 minutes. An operation that completed within the synchronous response window is never registered, so it does not appear here.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Return only operations in this state (an OperationState value). The match is case-sensitive, and an unrecognized value returns an empty list.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Return only operations of this command kind. The match is case-sensitive, and an unrecognized value returns an empty list.

200.description: Lists async operations, newest first: those still running and those that finished within about the last 60 minutes. An operation that completed within the synchronous response window is never registered, so it does not appear here.

get.description: Returns the current state of an async operation. This is a non-blocking snapshot: an unfinished operation is RUNNING, so poll until state is SUCCEEDED or FAILED. Returns 404 for an unknown id, for an operation that completed within the synchronous response window (it is never registered), and for one that finished more than about 60 minutes ago.

post.description: Replaces a single dashboard with the submitted Tableau XML, leaving the workbook's other sheets intact. A missing or empty body is rejected with 400 and a non-XML Content-Type with 415. A non-empty XML body that is not well-formed, or that the product cannot load into a valid workbook, is rejected with 422. The payload is NOT validated against the schema; use POST /v0/workbook/document:validate for XSD validation. This apply is unconditional last-writer-wins: it performs no precondition/If-Match check and will overwrite a concurrent edit to the same sheet. The apply is rejected with 409 when the submitted payload's sheet name does not match the target sheet's current name -- for example, if you renamed the sheet in the payload, or another editor renamed it after you read the document -- or when the name-matching payload element is the wrong sheet subtype (a story, <dashboard type='storyboard'>, where the target is a dashboard). A client error found while the apply completes synchronously returns a Problem Details response with code operation-failed carrying the underlying tableauErrorCode. Any other failure, including any failure of an apply that returns 202, is reported as a FAILED operation. An id that resolves to a sheet of a different kind returns 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

parameters.name: X-Tableau-Effective-Payload-Version
parameters.description: Reserved for future Tableau payload (file-format) version negotiation. Currently accepted but ignored: documents are always served and applied at the running product version.

requestBody.description: The dashboard's Tableau XML -- either the bare <dashboard> element returned by GET .../dashboards/{id}/document, or that element inside a <workbook> envelope. Only the dashboard whose name matches the target sheet's name is applied, and any other sheets in the payload are ignored. Top-level <datasources> definitions in the payload are ignored, but the applied dashboard's datasource references must still resolve to a datasource already present in the open workbook -- a reference to an absent datasource is rejected with 409.

get.description: Renders a single dashboard (resolved by id) as an image, returned inline as base64 or written to a caller-supplied file path. The id must resolve to a dashboard: an id that matches no sheet returns 404, and an id that resolves to a non-dashboard sheet or to a dashboard that is not yet renderable returns 409.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Path to write the image to. Must be absolute and name a file; a directory, a trailing slash, or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with a 400. When set, the response projects this path instead of inline base64; when omitted, the image is returned as base64.

parameters.name: mimeType
parameters.description: Requested image MIME type (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg, image/svg+xml). Defaults to image/png; an unsupported type also falls back to image/png. The effective type is returned in the response.

200.description: Renders a single dashboard (resolved by id) as an image, returned inline as base64 or written to a caller-supplied file path. The id must resolve to a dashboard: an id that matches no sheet returns 404, and an id that resolves to a non-dashboard sheet or to a dashboard that is not yet renderable returns 409.

post.description: Deletes the sheet identified by id, whatever its kind. Worksheets that were hidden because the dashboard was their only use become visible again. An id that matches no sheet yields a FAILED operation. Unlike the Tableau UI, this endpoint does not guard the workbook's last visible sheet; do not delete it, as removing it can leave the workbook with no visible sheets.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

post.description: Creates one blank dashboard with a generated name and makes it the active sheet. The response does not include its id, so list the dashboards to find it. Any request body is ignored.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: 0-based tab position at which the new dashboard(s) are inserted, shifting the existing tab at that position (and beyond) to the right. index=0 inserts before the first tab. To append at the end (make it the last tab), omit the parameter or use a value >=n (where n is the current number of tabs). Negative values also append at the end.

post.description: Replaces a single worksheet with the submitted Tableau XML, leaving the workbook's other sheets intact. A missing or empty body is rejected with 400 and a non-XML Content-Type with 415. A non-empty XML body that is not well-formed, or that the product cannot load into a valid workbook, is rejected with 422. The payload is NOT validated against the schema; use POST /v0/workbook/document:validate for XSD validation. This apply is unconditional last-writer-wins: it performs no precondition/If-Match check and will overwrite a concurrent edit to the same sheet. The apply is rejected with 409 if the submitted payload's sheet name does not match the target sheet's current name -- for example, if you renamed the sheet in the payload, or another editor renamed it after you read the document. A client error found while the apply completes synchronously returns a Problem Details response with code operation-failed carrying the underlying tableauErrorCode. Any other failure, including any failure of an apply that returns 202, is reported as a FAILED operation. An id that resolves to a sheet of a different kind returns 404.

post.description: Exports the open workbook to a non-native format, leaving the open document unchanged. Both filePath and format are required. format selects what to produce: "pdf" (a PDF of every sheet), "powerpoint" (a .pptx with one slide per sheet), "packaged-workbook" (a .twbx bundling the workbook and its data), or "prior-version" (a down-saved copy for an older Tableau release). filePath must end in the extension that format produces (.pdf, .pptx, .twbx, or .twb/.twbx respectively) or the request is rejected. For "prior-version", also supply targetVersion as the customer-facing release string (e.g. "2024.1"); an unrecognized version is rejected. The export always writes to the supplied filePath and never opens a dialog, so it is fully headless.

post.description: Saves the open workbook. Omit filePath, or send an empty or non-string filePath, to save in place at the path the workbook already has. Supply a filePath to Save As: the workbook is written to that path and the open document is re-pointed at it, so later saves go there (use exportAs for a copy that leaves the open document unchanged). filePath must end in .twb or .twbx: save writes workbook content verbatim without converting, so any other extension is rejected rather than writing a mislabeled file. The save is headless whenever the workbook has a writable path to save to -- a supplied filePath, or the existing path of an already-saved workbook whose file can be written. It cannot be headless when there is no writable existing path and no filePath is supplied: a workbook that has never been saved, a workbook whose existing file is read-only, or a workbook recovered from an autosave draft. In those cases the product opens its native Save As dialog, which blocks until a person responds, and cancelling that dialog still reports SUCCEEDED. The product may also show an upgrade prompt when saving a workbook from an older version.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. Structured extension members, such as tableauErrorCode, may appear as additional top-level fields.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error identity clients branch on.

Operation.description: The state of a dispatched operation. A command that fails is reported here with state FAILED and an error, still with HTTP 200 unless the route documents a 4xx status for that failure.

WindowInfo.description: A visible modal window or dialog in Tableau Desktop, observed at read time. Whether a client must act on it is conveyed by the containing response: dialogs and blockingWindows contain windows that need a human decision, while progressWindows contains self-clearing windows. The content fields (messageText, informativeText, detailedText, iconLevel, buttons, actions) are best-effort: standard message boxes expose them precisely, while other dialogs are read from their visible labels, read-only text areas, and buttons and may include incidental text.

detailedText.description: Diagnostic text capped to 1048576 UTF-8 bytes (1 MiB). When shortened, detailedTextTruncated is true.

DialogAction.description: A dialog capability descriptor. It contains no selected file, color, or printer payload.

DashboardRefreshOutcome.description: Per-worksheet dashboard refresh result. A PARTIAL or FAILED outcome is retained on a FAILED operation; successful worksheet refreshes are not rolled back.

StoryboardRefreshOutcome.description: Aggregate refresh outcome for the storyboard's current point, with per-worksheet visual results. A PARTIAL or FAILED outcome is retained on a FAILED operation; successful worksheet refreshes are not rolled back.

DialogActionInvocation.description: One exact action selected from a dialog's capabilities. File paths, printer choices, and color values are input-only and are not echoed.

DialogIdentity.description: Exact current-dialog identity copied from one DialogList item. sessionId and revision prevent a stale action from selecting a replacement dialog with the same visible text.

DialogList.description: Current registered Qt and native dialog observations. A false uiSnapshotAvailable value means the UI capture was bounded before completion and dialogs is not evidence of no blockers.

InvokeDialogActionRequest.description: Selects one current actionable dialog and one visible action by exact values from DialogList.

InvokeDialogActionResult.description: The request status and current dialog snapshot. Selection payloads are never echoed.

WorksheetItem.description: A worksheet in the open workbook.

index.description: The sheet's workbook-wide tab position, or null when the sheet is hidden.

DashboardItem.description: A dashboard in the open workbook.

index.description: The sheet's workbook-wide tab position, or null when the sheet is hidden.

StoryboardItem.description: A storyboard in the open workbook.

index.description: The sheet's workbook-wide tab position, or null when the sheet is hidden.

storyPointCount.description: The number of story points in the storyboard, or null when unavailable.

WorkbookInventory.description: Metadata and sheet inventory of the open workbook.

WorksheetInvalidField.description: One invalid field used by a worksheet and its native location.

WorksheetDiagnostics.description: Native used-field diagnostics for one worksheet. Status reports coverage: complete includes an invalidFields list, while partial or unavailable must not be treated as a clean result. invalidFields is omitted when status is unavailable, and message is present only when there is something to report.

OperationList.description: Async operations. List entries omit each operation's `result` and per-operation `blockingWindows`: fetch GET /v0/operations/{id} for an operation's `result`, and read blocking-window state once from the top-level `blockingWindows` here.

DatasourceItem.description: A datasource in the open workbook.

type.description: The datasource's backend kind, independent of whether it is an extract (see isExtract).

isExtract.description: True if the datasource is currently backed by an extract rather than a live connection.

hasDownloadFilePermission.description: Whether the current user has server permission to download the published datasource file (the Download/Save a Copy permission). Not whether the data can be queried or extracted. null for a datasource that is not published, where the permission does not apply.

ImageExport.description: The result of exporting a sheet as an image.

SummaryData.description: Tabular worksheet data as columns and rows. Returned by both the summary-data and underlying-data endpoints; the shape is identical for each.

LogicalTableItem.description: A logical table available for a worksheet's data.

ValidationResult.description: The outcome of validating a workbook document.

ShowMeRequest.description: The Show Me visualization to apply to a worksheet.

showMeType.description: The serialized Show Me visualization type to apply.

dataSource.description: Optional internal datasource name used to resolve selected fields.

fieldsSelectedInSchemaViewer.description: Optional fully qualified encoded field names, each with at least a datasource and field component. An explicit empty array supplies an empty field selection; omission preserves ambient selection.

ShowMeOptions.description: Context-sensitive Show Me options from Tableau's current native model. Options preserve native order and feature gating.

options.description: Every option offered by the current native Show Me model, in native order, including inapplicable options.

ShowMeWorksheet.description: The worksheet evaluated by the native Show Me model.

ShowMeOption.description: A visualization option from the current native Show Me model.

showMeType.description: The runtime visualization token from Tableau's current native Show Me model. The offered token set remains governed by native feature gating.

isApplicable.description: Whether the native Show Me model can apply this option to the worksheet and selected fields.

vizHasRequiredFields.description: Whether the current visualization supplies the fields required by this option.

dataSourceHasRequiredFields.description: Whether the current datasource supplies the fields required by this option.

helpUrl.description: The help URL supplied by the current native Show Me model.

ValidateCalculatedFieldRequest.description: The calculated-field formula to validate on a worksheet.

formula.description: The calculated-field formula text to validate.

CalculatedFieldValidationError.description: A validation error located within the calculated-field formula.

ValidateCalculatedFieldResponse.description: The outcome of validating a calculated-field formula.

SortRequest.description: The sort to apply to a field on the worksheet.

fieldName.description: The on-shelf field to sort, given as its field-instance name qualified by its datasource caption, in the form [Datasource Caption].[field-instance] (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[none:Ship Mode:nk]"). The base column name (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[Ship Mode]") will not match any field on the view and the sort is silently ignored.

direction.description: Sort direction; defaults to 'asc' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

sortType.description: Sort type; defaults to 'data-source-order' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

clearSort.description: When true, removes the existing sort on `fieldName` instead of applying one; `fieldName` is still required.

StartPageVisibility.description: Whether the Tableau Desktop start page is visible.

filePath.description: Path to save the workbook to (Save As); must end in .twb or .twbx. Omit, or send an empty value, to save the workbook in place at its current path.

ExportAsWorkbookRequest.description: What to export and where to write it.

filePath.description: Path to write the export to. Must be absolute and name a file; a directory, a trailing slash, or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with a 400. Its extension must match format: .pdf for pdf, .pptx for powerpoint, .twbx for packaged-workbook, and .twb or .twbx for prior-version.

format.description: The export format that selects what file to produce. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

targetVersion.description: Required when format is prior-version: the customer-facing Tableau release to down-save to (e.g. "2024.1"). Ignored for other formats.

isFullRefresh.description: Force a full refresh instead of an incremental one. Defaults to false: incremental when the extract supports it, otherwise a full refresh.

ApiRoot.description: API versions and the resource link map.

AppState.description: One app-wide point-in-time snapshot of Desktop activity and modal state. Window arrays are not attributed to an operation. When state is BLOCKED, blockedBy reports the strongest observed signal in precedence order: MODAL_DIALOG, the first active activity in canonical order, PROGRESS_DIALOG, MODAL_LOOP, then UI_UNRESPONSIVE.

state.description: IDLE only after a complete UI snapshot observes no activity, modal loop, or modal window; otherwise BLOCKED.

blockedBy.description: Present when state is BLOCKED and identifies the strongest observed signal.

uiSnapshotAvailable.description: Whether modal-loop and window evidence was captured within the bounded UI probe interval. A false value never produces IDLE and window arrays are omitted.

activeActivities.description: All active native activities in canonical order: LOADING, QUERYING, EXTRACT_REFRESH, DOWNLOADING, SERVER_COMMUNICATION.

CapabilityMatrix.description: Capabilities keyed on operationId. An operationId missing from the map is not part of this API version's public contract.

requiresServer.description: Whether a connected Tableau Server or Cloud session is required.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed. The code field identifies the specific problem, such as a missing required header or an unreadable body.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token was missing or invalid. The response carries a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

Forbidden.description: The request origin was not permitted.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist. The code field distinguishes an unknown route from a valid resource with an unknown id.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but does not support this HTTP method.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, such as an unsupported payload version.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request Content-Type is not accepted by this endpoint.

MisdirectedRequest.description: The request Host header was not a loopback address.

UnprocessableContent.description: The request was well-formed but semantically invalid and could not be applied, such as a document whose structure the product rejects. The code field identifies the specific problem.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The External Client API is disabled or shutting down.

Accepted.description: The command did not settle within the synchronous window. The body is the pending operation; poll the Location URL until it reaches a terminal state.

Location.description: Relative URL of the operation to poll.

UserAgent.name: User-Agent
UserAgent.description: Identifies the calling client as an RFC 9110 product token, such as my-client/1.2.0. Requests without a non-empty User-Agent are rejected with missing-user-agent.
